method: Generated original atlases, alpha cleanup, measured crop boundaries and one anatomical scale per identity. No tree falls or human poses were drawn procedurally.

prompts.pine:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: one pixel art destructible PINE TREE animation atlas for GREYLINE 2D side view war game. Input reference is STYLE reference only. Match its realistic rough bark, muted dark olive foliage, crisp visibly stepped pixel clusters; not cartoon, not soft painted. Subject only pine tree, no building, no people, no environment.
Exactly 4 columns x 3 rows =12 equal cells, widescreen canvas about 2048x1152. No grid lines, no labels, no text. Transparent alpha background. Each cell has ample blank padding. Every frame shows the SAME tree at the SAME anatomical scale; original full tree height about 235 pixels within each cell. Stump/root origin MUST be fixed at x=100,y=330 relative to every cell. Do not resize or squeeze the tree as it falls. Whole crown and branches must stay within their own cell even when horizontal.
Read frame order left to right, top to bottom:
0 healthy upright tall asymmetrical pine, dense layered needles, brown tapering trunk.
1 SAME upright tree, HALF DAMAGED: ragged crown missing several branch masses, splintered branches, bark wounds, much foliage still present, trunk upright.
2 start collapse: trunk freshly broken near root, crown leaning 8 degrees RIGHT.
3 fall phase: 18 degrees RIGHT from upright, wood fibers bending at broken stump.
4 fall phase: 30 degrees RIGHT, lower branches shedding small twigs.
5 fall phase: 43 degrees RIGHT, silhouette clearly diagonal.
6 fall phase: 57 degrees RIGHT, heavy crown lower.
7 fall phase: 71 degrees RIGHT, branches beginning to deform as they approach ground.
8 fall phase: 83 degrees RIGHT, low branch tips touching invisible ground baseline.
9 fall phase: 90 degrees RIGHT, horizontal trunk impacts ground, branches crumple naturally and a few needles fall. Tiny local wood fragments only, no dust cloud.
10 final fallen tree: independently drawn resting horizontal broken trunk connected visually to short jagged stump on left, damaged crown to RIGHT, visible crushed bent branches under trunk, grounded debris. This must make low solid cover, not a flattened green ellipse.
11 final alternative more damaged fallen pine with fewer needles and clearly exposed fallen trunk; same stump and footprint.
The falling frames must show genuine changed drawing and branch deformation, not the identical upright silhouette mechanically rotated. Preserve trunk length throughout. No baked ground tile, no fire, no smoke, no broad shadow. Serious realistic game pixels, transparent background, no checker pattern painted into RGB.
prompts.broadleaf:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: one destructible BROADLEAF OAK TREE pixel-animation atlas for GREYLINE, companion to a pine atlas. Input reference is STYLE reference only. Match realistic rough graybrown bark and muted olive small-leaf canopy, distinct hard pixel clusters, serious late-1990s side-view military game look. Only one tree identity shown through animation, not the building or pine reference.
Exactly 4 columns x 3 rows = 12 equal well separated cells on widescreen canvas. Transparent alpha backdrop, no floor, no broad shadow, no text, no labels, no grid. Do not clip foliage at any cell edge. Same physical tree height and trunk length in all frames; adult oak with spreading irregular crown. Upright full tree uses roughly 75 percent cell height. A stable broken stump at a fixed relative cell ground point stays in every falling frame. Fallen crown lies toward RIGHT; trunk must retain full original length and settle naturally, not squeezed or rescaled.
Frame reading left-to-right row-by-row:
0 complete upright mature broadleaf tree, asymmetrical branching round crown.
1 visibly HALF-DAMAGED but still upright: remove 40 percent of leaf masses, exposed snapped upper branches, splinter wounds and ragged gaps, original trunk remains.
2 collapse starts 6 degrees from vertical RIGHT: severe lower-trunk break, crown starts moving, split wood fibers.
3 17 degrees RIGHT: initial fall.
4 29 degrees RIGHT: accelerating fall, a couple detached small twigs.
5 43 degrees RIGHT: diagonal trunk, crown branches bending.
6 57 degrees RIGHT: clear continued progression, lowest crown twigs compress.
7 71 degrees RIGHT: almost down.
8 83 degrees RIGHT: low canopy first meets ground.
9 90 degrees RIGHT: impact, some crushed branches, small leaf fragments immediately around tree.
10 final grounded wreck: fallen brown trunk from jagged stump on left into damaged crown on right, small broken limbs and leaves, low bumpy natural cover. Do not flatten tree into an oval and do not keep a rigid rotated copy of the full upright crown.
11 alternate final wreck with thinner remaining leaves, same length, visibly broken branches.
Each pose must be a separately drawn physical intermediate, with trunk hinge motion and secondary branch bending. Whole shapes clear at game display height140 pixels. Opaque artwork with real transparent background, no checkerboard baked in.
